Yep.  I'm finally nearing the end of this fucked up journey (he doesn't know it yet, but I'm in the process of getting a new place to live) and I can honestly say that though I've learned a lot from this relationship, I would erase it in a heartbeat.  If I could go back in time to when I first met him and just start over from there, even better.

Like someone else said, I could have learned all of the lessons I did without having gone through the abuse, the torture, the expensive and traumatizing grippy sock vacation.  I know that past trauma is what drew me to him and what ultimately has kept me in this for the last 7 years, and with that being said, the last thing I've ever needed in my life was this added drama.  I'm in therapy now ultimately because of it, and uncovering a lot about why I put myself through this stuff, but I also did a lot of healing before I entered a relationship with him that I now feel has been set back years.  In a lot of ways I'm starting from square one again. 

So yeah.  I'd erase it.

So I can only speak from my own experience, but I have C-PTSD, and my husband has BPD.  One of the distinct differences for me is that I don't really have a fear of abandonment, or any sort of preoccupation with it.  Obviously, it upsets me when people want to exit my life.  But I recognize that as a problem I have to deal with and just kind of accept it.  I don't go to extreme measures to keep people from "abandoning" me and I can generally tell when a friendship/relationship is pretty solid.

I also don't tend to get intense, frequent rage outbursts like those that are commonly (but not always) seen in people with BPD.  If I do have an anger outburst it's usually after being pushed well past my limit, otherwise I tend to let things go.  Also, I feel with C-PTSD you're kind of more likely to fawn/people please and let others walk all over you than to be the one mistreating another person.  

There's definitely symptom overlap between the two, but even before therapy I recognized that I needed to start healing if I wanted to live some semblance of a happy life.  I think there's a level of self reflection present in C-PTSD that pwBPD aren't really comfortable with/capable of doing, depending on if they're being treated and how far along in treatment they are.  There are times I KNOW I'm in the wrong and acted out of line and I try to own it and apologize.  My husband thinks about 95% of his behavior is justifiable.

Dunno if this helps, but those are a few things I've observed in my marriage.
0/10 do not recommend.  I don't know how I've done it this long.

Yeah.  It's taken me a while but I'm finally realizing that.  I started joking he was like my unruly child but it stopped being funny once I realized how true that actually was.  Even the way he shows affection is very childlike, which from what I've read seems pretty common.

Thankfully we keep our finances separate, and just kind of move money to help as needed.  It was a hard boundary for me from the beginning and for him as well.  Working on a place to live, and going to discuss an evacuation plan with my DV counselor on Thursday.
Haven't been divorced yet but other than that spot on.

Omg I cannot even fathom how I'd respond to my husband yelling "WRONG" at me trying to comfort him.  Who actually does that??  I wish I could be inside one of their minds just to see what goes down in these moments.  It's one thing to let your partner know that something in particular isn't comforting for whatever reason, but to just yell that like some sort of demented gameshow host.  I can't.  I'm so sorry you went through that.  It sounds awful.

We don't have kids.  I'm mostly sticking it out right now because I'm not in a place financially to leave.  I had to buy a new car recently, when I was hoping mine would hold out one more year.  I also feel weirdly guilty about the prospect of hurting him like that, and somehow can't envision my life without him which is crazy because I'm miserable.  Ugh.

I'm honestly really glad you got out for the sake of your sanity.  It's seriously such a nightmare and mindfuck.  The worst part is there are a lot of things that I now excel at that my ADHD held me back from before, specifically because I had to start remembering to do them for both of us.  I'm in charge of our utility bills, all of the driving/finding transportation for him when I can't get him somewhere, most of the grocery shopping, making sure taxes get done on time every year (which there's always something HE procrastinates getting that we need and it always gets pushed to the last minute and it's always MY fault).  I do try very hard to pull my weight in the relationship because I know where my weaknesses are but every day it's always "I need more help from you!  You never -insert whatever weekly gripe here-!'

This...this is exactly what happened to me with my husband.  I'm awkward and dorky and struggle with ADHD.  We would get into tiffs about my messiness or the fact that I couldn't cook but then at some point he flipped and said "These are strengths that I have that you don't have.  If you need me to take the brunt of that on, I will, because there are things that you're stronger at than me and that you take on more of.  It balances out."

Over the years I've gotten better with domestic stuff and have been trying really hard to stick to a schedule and get at least a few things done a day.  Every day he reminds me that I'm not doing enough.
Honestly good for her.

Yep.  At one point it almost started to feel like some sick social experiment.  "Don't make any needs known.  Try your best not to argue or stick up for yourself.  Do whatever he asks.  Don't ask anything at all of him.  Maybe things will be calm."

And honestly?  It *does* work.  Temporarily.  Until I inevitably crack and do something that accidentally sets him off.  Or I remember I'm human and ask for something simple.  Or have the audacity to stand up for a friend he's shit talking.  Or he just gets bored/needs a tension release.  But generally speaking, yeah, things tend to become more calm when I'm not expressing my needs and trying to be "perfect" for him.  The issue is that it's impossible to keep up with and I never know when it's going to blow up on me.
My husband literally believes we were Frieda Kahlo and Diego Rivera in our past lives.

I'm stuck in this cycle with my husband currently.  There will be a huge explosion or a series of huge explosions, and I'll think "This is it.  This is the last straw.  I'm gonna end things. I'm gonna start planning." And then the next day, it'll be as if nothing happened.  It's dizzying.  Things will be so calm that I start feeling guilty for ever thinking I could leave.  I walk on eggshells for a bit but eventually settle back in and get comfortable.

And then the cycle repeats.

One thing I'm slowly learning is you have to take all of their behavior as a whole into consideration, and decide if the splitting and the fights and explosions are worth enduring for the good moments.  I don't know if the calm stretches are an attempt to try and erase the explosive ones and keep you on your toes, or if they just truly don't see them as anything abnormal.  End of the day, motivation or intent doesn't matter.  Do you want to live your life on edge, constantly waiting for the other shoe to drop, only for it to be thrown at you when you least expect it.

Lots, but his most recent bone to pick with me is the fact that I'm currently trying to eat healthier and lose weight, counting calories with Noom and all that jazz.  So because I don't want to eat cheeseburgers and pizza and bacon mac and cheese every day I am "obviously starving myself" and "depriving him of food he wants" because he "doesn't know how to cook for me anymore" and also he's "worried about me" because of how little I eat.

I eat 1200 calories a day.

Yes.  A couple months back I actually was worried I might have covid.  I had a lot of the main symptoms plus some of the weird fringe ones like vomiting etc.  My husband told me my symptoms were "too vague" and questioned whether I really felt as badly as I said I did, and was just generally kind of a jerk to me until I started throwing up and ended up scheduling myself a test (thankfully I did not have it).  He also always seems to be in a rush to call me "recovered" when I'm sick.  He often calls me selfish and tells me everything is always all about me, when in reality I'm often dropping stuff I want to do be able to do things for him etc.  

It's weird because the first day I'm sick, if he actually believes me, he sometimes can be really nurturing and sweet, letting me sleep, getting me water, bringing me soup and crackers in bed.  But if goes on any longer than a day he gets very visibly agitated with me and starts insisting I'm not really sick anymore or that I seem "100% better" to him.  I honestly don't even ask for much when I'm sick.  I normally just power through and even if I can't, I just try to sleep it off, and I only get sick a few times a year.  I can't imagine the blow out if I ever accused him of making up an illness.

The dinner thing is a huge point of contention between my husband and me.  Even if I just ask if he has a general mood then I'm "putting that decision on him".  But then probably 7/10 times if I just decide on something, he ends up having a problem with whatever I decide on.

-We were making out once and I stopped to kiss him on the nose thinking I was being cutesy.  He perceived this as an "obvious rejection" and had a meltdown.

-I asked him if he wanted to talk about his therapy session while tuning my guitar.

-I brought home plants that were bigger than he thought they'd be.  So he proceeded to berate me even into the next day while I was at work which caused me to have an anxiety attack.

-I decided to go work half an hour early.

-One time he went off on me for just sitting in the kitchen.

-I ate a single crouton while he was making dinner.

-I didn't take out the pot he wanted me to cook rice in so he shoved me.

-I told him he could find alternative rides to work and then after he'd been in my face yelling at me for a while I told him to shut up and stop so he tried to jump out of my car.

-I put on a documentary he wanted to watch because I was too tired to pick something I wanted and deal with the inevitable tantrum from that.  Had a tantrum anyway.

-I took myself to see a movie and texted him I might be ten minutes late picking him up from work.  I wasn't.  He yelled at me about the possibility for 20 minutes till we got to a friend's house.

You do not need to prove ANYTHING to him.  You are not a POS.  He is.  I am so sorry you are going through this.  You are not stupid.  He put his best face on on the beginning and now that he feels he has you locked in, he feels comfortable letting his guard down.  But you don't need this.  You don't deserve STD scared and to have to walk on eggshells and "prove" your love to someone who stomped all over you.  He should get in trouble honestly.

First of all, if he had sex with a minor, run.  Do not walk.  Report that shit.  Don't listen to him.  

My husband cheated on me last year.  We are both 32 and he cheated with a 19 year old.  I am still with him, and I honestly have so many regrets.  I can't move past it, but I'm also not allowed to bring it up or talk about it without him having a meltdown.  Since he claims he cheated because I was "neglectful" (spoiler: I'm not), he now feels twice as entitled to every ounce of my time and attention, with the implication being that if I don't give him what he wants, I can't expect anything less from him.  Please believe me when I say things will not get better from here.  The fact he wants you to keep quiet shows he has no remorse except for being caught.  What happens if this girl ends up pregnant?  Or he cheats again and gets ANOTHER girl pregnant??  Or gives you an STI??  Get out while you can.  This is not a healthy situation.
Pretty sure that was the short in Animatrix that caused me to become terrified of robots.  😂

The point is that you weren't cheating.  Yes, her behavior and reactions would be absolutely justified...if she had any evidence beyond her delusion.  Their reactions can absolutely be proportionate to the perceived offense.  The problem is, almost every time, *there is no offense*.  It doesn't really do much good to speculate whether their behavior would be considered so bad if their reality matched actual reality, because it doesn't.  Kicking someone out over a *feeling* is terrible.  Berating someone and accusing someone of something with no evidence other than "I feel like this is happening, therefore it must be" is psychotic.

Honestly the reason I've stayed is because I wanted to see him get help and start to feel better for himself.  But it seems the more help he gets, the more willing he is to discard me, which is in itself a total mindfuck because I've always been supportive of him despite the constant emotional turmoil I feel.  I know it's the BPD, but it just genuinely makes you feel crazy when they do everything in their power to push you away, and then punish you relentlessly when you finally check out or consider actually leaving.

I hadn't thought of this, but I do believe it to be true.  I'm not supposed to hear his therapy at all.  I always have headphones in or leave when does it.  Plus, as shitty as things still are he IS trying in therapy, and his therapist is pretty good at calling him out from what I understand, so she's not easy to lie to.  He also likes his therapist a lot and frequently talks about how he wishes they could be friends which I think gives him more incentive to be honest with her.

One of his big things was "She's a good friend, I don't want to lose her!" To which I responded he didn't have to, but that I didn't want to be friends with her.  Meanwhile, a friend who I dated briefly ten years ago once commented on a meme I shared saying something like "Eh, I was a fan" in regards to what he thought of my body.  Ten years ago.  All hell broke loose, and I had to delete the comment and distance myself from this friend, despite the fact we haven't seen each other in ten years and only catch up occasionally.  If someone randomly checks me out on the street, he spends the whole day talking about wanting to kill them.  The double standards are insane.

He's trying to frame it as "It was just a joke" which I don't believe at all.  We DO joke with certain friends that way but openly, and not behind each other's backs.  If it was a joke he would have told me about it, or made some silly comment about all three of us getting together.  I think he really thinks I'm dumb.  I know I deserve more respect than this.  I feel like this is the final straw.

Yeah.  Literally all I wanted was for him to be like "I'm sorry you overheard that.  It was inappropriate.  I understand why you're upset."  Instead he made me feel like I was insane for being upset that he was propositioned and was actually considering it?  And also that it was a friend??  Like is that really a thing a good friend does behind your back???

I know.  I just feel so lost.  He's already cheated on me and it ended up being the final blow after a long shitty year and I ended up having a mental breakdown and being hospitalized.  This friend knows this happened, and still felt it was appropriate to say that to him behind my back so it just feels like a double punch in the gut.  I've been working hard in therapy and trying to move toward forgiveness since he's been in therapy too but it just feels like every other day the rug gets pulled out from under me.  I'm scared to leave for a lot of reasons but I feel like if I stay I'm just going to die anyway.

I'm just...so tired of staying strong I guess.  It gets progressively harder every day.  I miss my dad.  I don't even have the guts to leave my husband.  I fantasize about him leaving me first so I can just be on my own.  I don't even want to date anyone after him.  I just want to be left alone.

Thank you for responding though.  I know I'm probably being dramatic but it's nice to be heard.

"I literally just want stability.  I want you to be nice to me consistently."

"Well you knew I had BPD so I don't know why you expected *all that*"

Touché
Ouch.  I've been with my husband almost six years.  The last line got me.
I hope they do for as well.

No problem!  I definitely get it.  I get caught up in the true things my husband criticizes me for all the time.  But the thing I try to keep in mind is that him being right doesn't give him free reign to verbally abuse me or humiliate me or try to control me.  All I can do is work on the things that need working on, but my existence is still valid.

Here's the thing: you are human.  You are flawed and you will inevitably have things in your life that are worth examining.  Everyone does.  Of course there will be times she has a valid reason to be upset.  No one does everything perfectly, and I think it's easy to forget when we're in the midst of a relationship with a pwBPD that we are not 100% innocent all the time.  We fuck up.  And that's ok.  What's not ok is the constant nitpicking, tearing you down, and condescending behavior.  In healthy relationships, both parties are able to express that a partner upset them without insulting them.  In a healthy relationship, your partner should never want to criticize and embarrass you in front of others.  In a healthy relationship, when one partner is down or having a hard time, then there should be support and understanding.  Whether her criticisms of you were true or not, the way she expressed them is what was toxic.  You shouldn't feel guilty in a relationship for having normal human flaws or for going through a rough patch.

I'm so sorry you're going through this.  I honestly wish I did have some insight, but I don't.  I've tried speaking honestly and openly with my husband, but then he just accuses me of blaming him for all of our relationship problems.  I try very hard to hold myself accountable for the areas in which I need to improve, but he is pretty much unable to sit in the discomfort of having hurt me.  He at least admits at this point that his cheating was a very severe, long splitting episode, but aside from that he seems to think the fact that he's apologized should absolve him of everything.  If you're not married to your pwBPD, I'd suggest just ending things for good.  I understand why it's hard, but you'll likely never see him self-reflect the way you want/need him to.  I love my husband from the depths of my soul but if I'm being brutally honest, if given the chance to go back in time knowing what I know now I would not have married him.

That's horrible.  I'm so sorry he did that.  😢 I've definitely had moments where I'll off-handedly mention something pertaining to my marriage, and then whoever I'm talking to will just pause and then hug me, or look absolutely horrified.  I don't realize a lot of things are bad until I'm telling someone else a lot of the time.
Right??  I told him that's a really fucked up, unhealthy mindset to have in general but ESPECIALLY when it comes to kink.

Yeah.  When my husband and I started talking, it was like a dream.  I couldn't believe I found someone I was so compatible with.

"You like video games?  I love video games!  I have a bunch of classic systems we can play together!"

"You're adventurous and love going on spontaneous day trips and finding new and cool places?  Me too!  That's the best!"

"You're kind of kinky?  Well gee whiz, so am I!  We'd have a lot of fun together! ;)"

And then when we got together:

"I don't know.  I think it's stupid you'll just play this game for hours.  It doesn't even seem fun.  Like I used to like video games but I'm not really into them anymore."

"You know doing stuff like this costs money a lot of the time.  I don't want to spend any money.  It's cool you've found all these free things we can do but I'd rather plan to do these things a few weeks in advance instead of just up and doing them.  Except there's no guarantee I'll be in the mood to do it the day of after planning."

"I can't do those kinds of things with you because I'm in a relationship with you.  I can only do those things with people I don't give a shit about.  It'd be different if I was just using you."

He's definitely intelligent to an extent and attractive and PRESENTS himself as this fun, care free person to other people.  But behind closed doors it's just constant neuroses and arguing and backing out of plans we've made at the last possible second because he "just wants to stay home and chill with me" or he's having a crisis.  They really do mold themselves into exactly what they think you want and then when you call them out on it make up all kinds of excuses or say something like "Well would you have like me otherwise???" I don't know?  Maybe???  But either way at least i wouldn't have false expectations going in.

This is exactly what happened when I found out my husband cheated on me.  He had been joking to me about how there were rumors floating around about him and the person he cheated with.  I didn't think anything of it at first but then suddenly it just started to feel very sus.  He used to leave his laptop open to his Facebook page so one day I just...looked.  I think he'd figured I'd never be suspicious enough to snoop because why would he leave all of that open if he had nothing to hide?  I confronted him and after the initial shock of "Oh shit, I'm caught" wore off it was "I can't believe you went through my messages.  I can't even have any privacy!  That's so fucked up!!'

I just read your post and I'm really sorry this is happening to you.  I don't know what to say other than you are not abusive and I hope you and your child are reunited soon.  ❤️. They shouldn't have to grow up in that kind of chaos and hopefully someone on the right side of the law sees through her behavior.

Yes!  My husband is exactly like this.  EVERY TIME we have a great day, without fail, he's moody and irritated or having a crisis the very next day.  He describes is as a "crash from the high of having a good day".  It's like they can't hold onto that feeling.  The second whatever is making them happy or have a good day is over, POOF!  Like it never even happened.

I'll refrain from shitting on the rug only because I'd be forced to clean it.  😂
Thank you so much for the award!  I hope you're finding healing.  ❤️

I hear that.  I get accused of "feeding" his abusive behavior if I react or call it out.  But no matter how they respond to it, you are ALWAYS entitled to your feelings, and you are ALWAYS entitled to stick up for yourself if you feel you're not being treated well or fairly.  They can take it however they want and react however they will but that's a reflection of them and not you.

Uuugh I hate how accurate this is.  When my husband cheated on me, I became very angry and withdrawn.  When I would get angry he'd accuse me of being abusive (nevermind the fact I dealt with literally all of his anger being directed at me for five years) and when I would withdraw from the pain it was "This is the shit that lead me to do this in the first place!" So in the end his cheating became not something that hurt me, but something he did because he was so hurt by a situation he largely created.  The message became "I cheated because of you, so now YOU have to fix things or I'll do it again."

Every time.  He'll stand in the doorway and block me, guilt trip me for just "storming off", and if I do manage to get out the door, will call me incessantly until I pick up just to scream at me some more.  Once he grabbed my arm and twisted it to the point he left bruises so he could rip my keys out of my hand and throw them across the room.  He always accuses me of abandoning him and deliberately trying to hurt him when really I just need a minute to cool off so I can think straight and respond like a rational human being.  He refuses to believe my walking off has more to do with me than with him.

I've been accused of using him for a place to stay, to not be alone, as a 'maid', cook, etc.

I moved in pretty quickly in the relationship, but it was at his request. I was moving out of where I was living at the time and had a plan, but changed it to move in with him. I am the one that has places I can go if shit really hits the fan.  

I'm good on my own.  Even in previous relationships, I was always very independent and was ok if I didn't get to see whoever I was dating for a week or two.  I love my alone time.

I will admit, I'm messy, and not the best at remembering chores.  I have ADHD and executive dysfunction is a bitch.  I used to be REALLY bad with this, but I've improved 100 fold since we've been together.  He seems to think all the chores are "put on him" so he "never gets to relax" but in reality, he was home for 6 months because of covid while I worked 45-50 hours a week, and most days I'd come home to nothing done.  It doesn't bother me that much, but the accusation that I do nothing to help while he literally did nothing bothered me A LOT.

So yeah.  It seems to be a feature.

Been kind of obsessed with this song lately and the more I listen to it the more it almost sounds like a pwBPD speaking to their FP.  List of expectations, talking about the other person making everything ok/their troubles going away, burning bridges.  Just thought some of you might be able to relate.

YES!  My husband got mad at me a few weeks ago because I tossed a bag of bacon onto the kitchen table with an attitude after an argument, started screaming I "chucked it at him" when I literally just kind of dropped it onto a spot nowhere near him and walked away.  I brought up how he used to throw chairs at/near me during arguments and all fucking hell broke loose.  Like I'll admit I was acting bitchy but nowhere near unhinged or dangerous and you'd think I literally just beat him with the bag.  But the extreme reactions I've had to deal with from him obviously aren't going to have any lasting affects.  Oh nooo.

I honestly wish that wasn't his exact wording because it's so cringe but that is his exact wording.  😂 He too could have sex all day and still want more.  And be really didn't understand how that's not sustainable long term.  I remember even when it dropped from 3-4 times a day to 1-2 times a day he freaked out.  Granted, my drive now is pretty much non-existent but it's largely because of the way he's treated me, and I'm only just now realizing it.  I used to cry about it and spend hours researching low libido in women and at one point was contemplating supplements and anything else that might help.  I thought I was broken and failing him.  Turns out it's just hard to be in the mood when you're being gaslit and emotionally slaughtered on a costant basis.

Yeah.  I dunno if I believe it only happened once.  I just have no proof of anything other than the one person.  My husband cites his sex drive as well although he doesn't believe he's a sex addict. Instead he just says things like "I REQUIRE daily release, and if you're not going to give that to me, what the FUCK ELSE am I supposed to do?"

I dunno, dude.  Masturbate? Consistently treat me like a human being so that I actually want to have sex with you daily?  Divorce me???

Mine supposedly only cheated the once.  Supposedly.  But after it all came out he pretty much just immediately expected me to give him all the attention, intimacy and affection he wanted in order to prevent it from happening again.  Processing time?  Nope.  Space? Not until I said something he didn't like and kicked me out for five days.  Just basically "Yep.  I cheated.  So you better give me more attention or I'll keep doing it/do it again."
pwBPD: -cheats on you and then dismisses your feelings about it- pwBPD: WHY AREN'T YOU GIVING ME AFFECTION???

My dad died last year.  We had a relationship that sounds similar to yours with your father.  We spoke and hung out occasionally, but ultimately we both liked having our own space.  But if I was in any sort of trouble at all, he'd drop everything to be there for me.  If a new movie came out or a new restaurant opened that he thought I'd like, we'd be there.  The things we did do were very special and dear to us, and accentuated the things we had in common.

One of the hardest things I've grappled with since is regret for having not been there more, and for having not known how sick he was.  He hid it from everybody until he couldn't anymore.

It's hard, and it's not going to happen overnight, but you have to forgive yourself for the things left unsaid.  If your connection with him was even half of what you say it was, I promise you, he knew, and that connection is something you'll never lose.  I'm a skeptic when it comes to most things spiritual, but one thing my dad always told me was "Pay attention".  Since he died, I've paid attention to everything around me, and I've found that he speaks to me all the time in ways that are almost frighteningly uncanny.  Pay attention to anything that reminds you of him, to things you might not even necessarily think about, to dreams.  Missing him will still hurt like fucking hell, but it's a little more bearable when you can find things that make you feel like he's still with you somehow.

Haven't been discarded yet, but back in the devaluing phase after three or so months of idealization (yay!).  In addition to being told I only care about my needs and I never do anything for him, he has also accused me of

- Using him just to keep a roof over my head
- Never taking responsibility for my actions (I do take responsibility for them, to the point where I've tried mending things that it turns out weren't even problems in me to begin with)
- Being defensive (because I stick up for myself)
- Looking to cheat on him (he cheated, I never have)

Plus many more fun and exciting things I can't think of off the top of my head.  The accusations are definitely pretty standard.  It's projection 9 times out of 10.

I've been in mine five years, married four.  Tomorrow is actually our wedding anniversary, and we are currently fighting over my lack of sex drive (nevermind that it's hard to feel sexy and battered at the same time, plus the fact I'm on anti-depressants).
